links.outcome: Compared LLMs (GPT-4, Llama 2) against traditional models on same test data for cognitive decline detection
links.effect: GPT-4 outperformed Llama 2 but did not outperform traditional models (hierarchical attention network, XGBoost); ensemble achieved precision 90.3%, recall 94.2%, F1 92.2%.
links.quote: GPT-4 demonstrated superior accuracy and efficiency compared to Llama 2, but did not outperform traditional models.

links.outcome: Model performance on local EHR data against annotated reference standard
links.effect: Models trained on local EHR data showed diverse error profiles; ensemble improved precision from 70%-79% to above 90%; only 2 of 63 errors (3.2%) were mutual across models.
links.quote: LLMs and traditional machine learning models trained using local EHR data exhibited diverse error profiles.

unlisted_practices: Majority-vote ensemble of LLM and traditional ML models to improve precision
Prompt engineering strategies (hard/soft prompting, error-analysis-based instructions) for clinical note classification

screen.reason: This study benchmarks LLMs (GPT-4, Llama 2) against traditional ML models and an ensemble method for extracting signs of cognitive decline from retrospective EHR clinical notes, focusing purely on model development and classification accuracy without testing deployment practices or safeguards.
